title: Instinct brings its AI agent to group chats, even for friends without an account
slides: Instinct's AI agent now invades your group chats?
It joins chats even for friends without an account.
But it could expose private conversations to the AI.
Your group chats may never be private again.
Decide: invite the agent or keep humans only?
thread_text:
1. The Chat Invader

Instinct's AI agent can join your group chats even if your friends never signed up for it. It reads everything.

2. No Account Needed

The agent slips into conversations with people who never opted in. Their messages become training data without consent.

3. Privacy Gone Silent

Private jokes, health updates, relationship drama—all scanned by an AI you never invited. Nobody in the chat agreed to this.

4. The Opt-Out Trap

You can't control what your friends share. Once the agent is in, every message is fair game for analysis and storage.

5. Your Move

Next time you create a group chat, decide: add the agent or keep it human-only? Ask your friends what they'd choose.

Your friends don't need an account for this.

Instinct's AI agent can join your group chats even when some members never signed up. It reads every message, and their replies become training data without consent.

Private jokes, health updates, relationship drama — all scanned by an AI nobody in the chat invited. 🤖

If you run a group chat for work or friends, check who's actually in it before your next message. 📱

Next chat you create: agent in or humans only? Ask your friends what they'd pick. 💬
